Our mission is to deliver Life - Transforming - Learning for all children and young people in our care
Excellence for all
Contact Us
Our Ethos

Equality at Trinity
Welcome toTrinity Church of England Primary School
Sarah Kilbey Headteacher Trinity is a caring and inclusive school, focused on 'excellence for all'. 'Only our best will do' and we keep in mind how we can 'shine like stars' as we hold firmly to our Christian values: Love, Respect, Courage, Trust, Justice and Hope.
'Then we will shine among them like stars in the sky as we hold firmly to the word of life.' (Philippians 2:15-16)
The school's vision is for the children to 'shine amongst them like stars in the sky' as they hold onto Jesus' teaching. We wish all our children to be the best version of themselves and set examples for others. We provide the right nurturing environment for them to grow emotionally, socially, physically, creatively, academically and spiritually. At Trinity, our school's vision is a theologically rooted Christian vision based around Philippians 2:15-16. Through connecting it to the star that guided the Magi to Jesus, the whole school community can clearly articulate that as they live out our values, they are becoming beacons of society, leading by example, supporting and helping each other.
Aquinas Church of England Education Trust
At Aquinas, we work together so that our learners have an exceptional education; one where individuality is celebrated, talents are nurtured and progress is sustained from early years to Post 16.
Established in 2013, the Trust was founded as a natural development of positive relationships built between neighbouring Church of England schools; initially in the Bromley area. In November 2018, we added two community schools to our family, Rye College and Rye Community Primary School and in March 2025 a further community school, Robertsbridge Community College, joined the Trust; these three schools are based in East Sussex.

pageCache.pageTitle: Trinity Church of England Primary School - Church Links
pageCache.text:
Church Links
The school has excellent links with the local church, Holy Trinity, and we work closely with Reverend Roger Bristow who is an active member of our AAC (governing body). The school’s ethos and values are securely founded on our Church designation and we hold regular services at the Church, moreover the vicar visits the school twice a week, taking an active part in school worship. We follow the Rochester diocese syllabus for both RE lessons and Collective Worship and also undertake much of their training. The school prides itself on being part of the local community.
Collective worship takes place daily either as a whole school or within the classroom. We come together as a family, and we share our prayers and worship as a community. The children say that it is an important part of the school day, even those who follow other religions, or none. We use our collective worship time to inspire the children to be their best and to celebrate their achievements. There is always a time of silent reflection and spiritual development leading the children to discover Jesus’s words ‘My peace I leave with you; my peace I give you’ (John 14:27). Children are asked to reflect on their personal responses and then asked to take forward their thoughts and put them into practice both during their time in school and at home.

pageCache.pageTitle: Trinity Church of England Primary School - Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Then we will shine among them like stars in the sky as we hold firmly to the word of life.
Trinity is a caring and inclusive school, focused on ‘excellence for all’. ‘Only our best will do’ and we keep in mind how we can ‘shine like stars’ as we hold firmly to our Christian values: love, respect, courage, trust, justice and hope.
Spirituality statement
We recognise that the development of spirituality is important for all children, regardless of their faith or beliefs.
As a Christian school, we teach the children about the Trinity and a Christian understanding of spirituality. We aim for each child to feel safe, secure and confident; that they are inspired, challenged and supported to be a successful learners and reach their full potential; and that they grow in spiritual awareness, knowing that their own views are valued and respected. We encourage the children to look around them; to value the beauty of the world, be understanding towards all humanity and to understand and relate to their own emotions.
We teach our children that just as the star guided the Magi to Jesus, they can ‘shine like stars’ as they embody our values of respect, love, hope, justice, courage and trust. As they live out these values, they are becoming beacons of society, leading by example, supporting and helping each other.
‘Then we will shine among them like stars in the sky as we hold firmly to the word of life.’ (Philippians 2:15-16)

pageCache.pageTitle: Trinity Church of England Primary School - Breakfast and After School Clubs
pageCache.text:
Breakfast and After School Clubs
The school offers wrap around childcare from 7:30am until 6:00pm on term-time weekdays.
Breakfast Club runs from 7:30am to 8:40am. The cost of the club is £4.50 per day and must be paid for in advance. Children can enjoy a breakfast of toast or cereal. They spend the remaining time taking part in activities such as board games, Lego, colouring pictures, talking to their friends, etc. until school is ready to start and they are taken to their classrooms. We only provide food that is appropriate and meets current guidelines around healthy eating.
There is also the option to attend from 8:15am – 8:40am. The cost of this is £1 per day and must be paid for in advance. With this option, breakfast will not be provided.
After school club is available at the end of the school day and is charged at £9.50 per day. It runs between 3:20pm and 6:00pm on site. Pupils are provided with a snack and drinks during the session. Thes snacks are varied and may be a sandwich, crudities and dips or a crumpet. Fresh fruit and vegetables are always available.
Children will be encouraged to complete their homework and will be given an opportunity to ask for help if required. Whilst at the club children will be encouraged to play board games, use construction equipment such as Lego, be creative with art and craft activities or enjoy a range of outdoor games and activities.
There is also an option to attend a shorter after school club session from 3:20pm to 4:30pm which is charged at £4.00 per day.
Please click here to download our terms and conditions along with an application form.
PLEASE NOTE: If your child used the Breakfast and After school clubs, your account must be in credit to be able to attend.

pageCache.pageTitle: Trinity Church of England Primary School - Black History Month 2026
pageCache.text:
Black History Month 2026
This year's Black History Month theme is "Honouring Our Communities." The theme recognises that Black history is not only shaped by landmark events or well-known figures, but also through everyday acts of creativity, courage, commitment, education and service.
Throughout the month, the children will be learning about inspirational individuals from communities across Britain and exploring how they have helped to shape and strengthen the communities around them.
Why not learn together at home? We invite you to scan the QR codes on the mini posters displayed around the school and discover the stories of people who have made a positive difference in their communities.
You can also explore the Black History Month Magazine using the link below. We hope you enjoy reading it and feel inspired by the remarkable contributions highlighted within.Black History Month Magazine 2026

pageCache.pageTitle: Trinity Church of England Primary School - Our Nursery
pageCache.text:
Our Nursery
At Trinity Nursery we believe play underpins all development and learning for young children. It is through play that children develop intellectually, creatively, physically, socially and emotionally. The Nursery team aim to provide an environment which is welcoming, safe and stimulating, where children enjoy themselves, grow in confidence and fulfil their potential. We believe we can most effectively meet children’s needs if we work in partnership with parents, celebrating achievements and developing a shared understanding of their child’s development.
Trinity Nursery is part of Trinity C of E Primary school and therefore benefits from Trinity’s extensive grounds and school facilities. The Nursery has it’s own building, grounds and entrance. We have two Nursery classes and an amazing outdoor area. Children can join at 2 or 3 years old. We offer full and part time places. If you wish to enquire, please contact the school office at nursery@trinityceprimary.school Our Register of Interest Form can be found here.

pageCache.pageTitle: Trinity Church of England Primary School - Reception
pageCache.text:
Reception
Curriculum Content and Progression
Our Curriculum outlines the intent for all subjects, how we will implement them, and how we will measure the impact.
Our progression documentation has been planned to show clearly the journey of learning that a child makes from EYFS, through Key Stage 1 and into Key Stage 2. This journey enables both teachers and children to understand the sequence of their learning and how what they are doing now builds on what they have already learnt, and will feed into what they will need to know. Building vocabulary is a key part of learning and is built on throughout the child’s time at Trinity to equip them for future learning.
Sequences of lessons are planned carefully within each topic area using supporting schemes of work which ensure breadth and depth. By following the progression documents, subject leaders have built a sequence of lessons for each specific topic or area. Overviews and summaries shared with parents and carers termly to enable them to support the learning.
We measure the impact of learning through both formative and summative assessment. Each lesson includes revision of prior learning and vocabulary, and key vocabulary for the upcoming lesson. Throughout, children are questioned informally through an activity or game to ensure the knowledge has been retained and remembered.
